values.title: Quickstart
values.summary: Create a project, define a table and run your first typed query in about ten minutes.
values.body:
## Before you start

You need Node.js 20 or later and a Tessera account. The CLI works on macOS, Linux and Windows (WSL).

## Build your first endpoint

1

Create a project

Run the create command. It scaffolds `schema.ts`, a `.env` file and a generated client folder.

Terminal

```
npm create tessera@latest my-app
cd my-app
```

2

Define a table

Open `schema.ts` and add a table. Columns are typed, and you can mark them as required, unique or give them a default.

schema.ts

```
import { table, uuid, text, boolean, timestamp } from "tessera"
 
export const todos = table("todos", {
  id: uuid().primaryKey(),
  title: text().notNull(),
  done: boolean().default(false),
  createdAt: timestamp().defaultNow(),
})
```

3

Push the schema

Tessera plans the migration, shows you the SQL and applies it to your development environment.

Terminal

```
npx tessera push
```

4

Query it

Import the generated client and read your first rows. The result is fully typed.

app.ts

```
import { db } from "./tessera"
 
const open = await db.todos.where({ done: false }).all()
// open: Todo[]
```

Development data

Your development environment starts empty. Use `npx tessera seed` to load sample rows from `seed.ts`.

## What you built

You now have a Postgres table, a migration history and a typed client. The same schema also powers the REST API, so `GET /v1/rows/todos` works straight away.
